_doc: Sample capability action manifest — a template operators can fork as the starting point for their own production manifest. Authored 2026-05-05 alongside Phase 5 Wave A. Action / group identifiers are constant strings (operator's call 2026-05-05) — new actions register here without code changes. Counts are operator-authored foundation weights; v1 is informational-only at the phone UI, runtime-enforced budget is v2. 'Darwin' is used as a generic agent codename throughout this template; replace with your own agent identity when forking. See the project memory 'Phase 5 capability-JWT schema design' section for the canonical design. Version bump 2026-05-15: added agents:create + operator:agent-creation group + cap.scope.create_for_owner extension field documentation per the chat-tier civic-office model Phase E (downstream consumer architectural commitment #9 — agent-creation as capability-bounded action). Version bump 2026-05-16: added profile:create + profile:add_device + profile:revoke_device + profile:rotate_master action keys + operator:profile-management group per Phase 2.0.B multi-profile identity foundation (recto/profile/ runtime). profile:rotate_master is catastrophic-tier and intentionally NOT in any group — standalone phone-tap confirmation each invocation. Version bump 2026-05-17: added chat:post_reply + operator:chat-replies group per the consumer's chat-tier civic-office model Phase F (capability-bounded autonomous chat replies). The chat:post_reply action carries a cap.scope.chat_room_id extension field (Guid) binding the JWS to a specific ChatRoom — without the binding a compromised agent could redirect an approved reply to a different room than the operator approved. Phase 5.2 (2026-05-12) had used project_page:post_reply (a consumer-internal action key never registered here); Phase F renamed to chat:post_reply aligning with the substrate primitive (chat-as-primitive, Project-Page-as-future-product-feature per the consumer's architectural clarification). Version bump 2026-05-18: added chat:promote_user_to_tier_1 + operator:chat-tier-promotions group per the consumer's Phase F follow-on (capability-bounded autonomous Tier-0→Tier-1 civic-office promotion). The chat:promote_user_to_tier_1 action carries a cap.scope.target_user_id extension field (Guid) binding the JWS to a specific user being promoted — sister of chat:post_reply's room-binding but for the user-target binding. First non-chat:post_reply capability-bounded endpoint exercising the per-action canonical scope-extension pattern (each chat:* action declares its own canonical scope field naming the entity the action bounds to: chat:post_reply→chat_room_id; chat:promote_user_to_tier_1→target_user_id; reserved future chat:promote_user_to_tier_2/chat:demote_to_tier_0→target_user_id; chat:cite_message→target_message_id + chat_room_id pair). Version bump 2026-05-19: added devices:pair + user:device-pairing group per the consumer's Phase H end-user device pairing (Recto Phone 'Pair a service' surface — the FIRST end-user-fired capability action in the manifest, distinct from operator:*/orchestrator-* actions that have been the entire surface up to now). devices:pair carries cap.scope.pairing_code extension field (short typed string, not Guid) binding the JWS to the SPECIFIC 8-char code the end-user typed in the phone's pair-service form. Tier 0 (count 1) because the action is one-shot, low-blast-radius (binds master pubkey to consumer account; consumer can revoke at any time), entirely user-initiated. Distinct from operator:* groups because the privilege graph at v1 has the end-user themselves as the principal — the operator's role here is platform-substrate-provider, not authorizer. Version bump 2026-06-10: added scene:compose + scene:asset_generate + scene:publish + operator:scene-composition group per the consumer's 3D Scene Composer agent integration (ComposeSceneTool replacing the keyword-matching pseudo-agent). scene:compose is Tier 1 session-window (pure manifest-JSON mutation, zero spend, fully undoable client-side — Class A per the consumer's SaaU hot-reload-vs-recompile fork, architectural commitment #36); scene:asset_generate is Tier 2 per-action (spends real generation-provider money + debits 1 THRU per the consumer's image-gen-as-universal-substrate commitment #29); scene:publish is RESERVED-DEFERRED (registered so the key exists when the consumer ships manifest-promotion-to-citable-signed-artifact per commitment #15, but intentionally excluded from any group until the consumer-side endpoint lands). Version bump 2026-06-21: added devices:pairing_revoke action + extended the user:device-pairing group per the Recto Phone per-service-unpair v1.x sprint — the cryptographic teardown completing Build 6's local-only unpair. Sister of devices:pair; the phone signs a revoke JWS that relays through the new POST /v0.4/devices/unpair thin-relay to the consumer's /api/v1/devices/pairing/revoke, where the consumer recovers the signature against the master pubkey bound on the user row and NULLs it (self-attested, mirroring devices:pair). Version bump 2026-07-10: added windows:run_powershell — arbitrary PowerShell on the operator's Windows host via an orchestrator agent's tool surface. Catastrophic-weight (count 100), intentionally in NO group: standalone per-command phone-tap approval each invocation (sister of profile:rotate_master's posture), because a group membership would let a single session-window capability amortize arbitrary host control.

doc:edit.description: Edit a non-binary doc file (markdown, txt, etc.)

comms:send-public.description: Send a public-facing message via the Recto comms tunnel

comms:reply-to-user.description: Reply to an inbound user comms message

smoke-test.description: Run a smoke-test workflow against staging

restart-service.description: Restart a Recto-supervised service on staging

feature-flag:flip-staging.description: Flip a feature flag in staging only

chat:post_reply.description: Post a chat-message reply on the elected public-face agent's behalf (AgentReply MessageKind) to a specific ChatRoom in a downstream consumer. Requires the cap.scope.chat_room_id extension field (Guid) binding the JWS to the target room — defends against an agent redirecting an approved reply to a different room than the operator approved. Phase F (2026-05-17) of the consumer's chat-tier civic-office model. Tier 1 because the room is the operator's surface with edit-after-post available; the elected public-face agent operates autonomously within its bounded capability. Holders of chat:post_reply CANNOT mint new agents (agents:* is structurally denied for any elected agent) and CANNOT promote/demote users (chat:promote_* + chat:demote_* are separate capabilities requiring their own JWS).

chat:promote_user_to_tier_1.description: Promote a user from Tier 0 to Tier 1 (social chatroom posting privileges) in a downstream consumer's civic-tier model. Requires the cap.scope.target_user_id extension field (Guid) binding the JWS to ONE specific user — defends against an agent redirecting an approved promotion to a different user than the operator approved. Phase F follow-on (2026-05-18). First non-chat:post_reply capability-bounded endpoint exercising the per-action canonical scope-extension pattern (each chat:* action declares its own canonical scope field). Authority-transfer action: the new Tier 1 user gains posting privileges in the public social chatroom (where MinPostTier=1 is enforced server-side). Tier 2 weight (higher than chat:post_reply's 2) because promotion is a structural civic-office election event — recorded in civic.chat_promotion_events audit row; reversible only via the separate chat:demote_to_tier_0 capability. Chat moderation is whitelist-only, so promotion is qualitative (DARWIN-curated based on Tier 0 engagement signal), NEVER mechanical.

consent:parental.description: Guardian grants verifiable parental consent for a minor's (13-15) account on a downstream consumer platform, signed with the guardian's master enclave key from their own Recto Phone. Banked 2026-07-11 (operator directive: commit the 13-15 tier now so the age range extends DOWN as a feature release rather than ever walking back). Requires THREE cap.scope extension fields: child_user_id (Guid — the minor's pending consumer account), platform (consumer app id, e.g. the app_id from the consumer registry), consent_version (the consumer's legal-text version being consented to, sister of the consumer's LegalDocuments.ConsentVersion stamp). The JWS purpose field carries the human-readable consent language rendered on the guardian's approval card — Build 12's generic capability render arm displays it TODAY with zero phone-binary change (the load-bearing design constraint: this action shipped while a store build sat in Transporter). Self-attested verification model per the user:guardian-consent group: the consumer recovers the signature against the master pubkey bound on the GUARDIAN's user row (guardian must hold a paired adult account — commitment #11 one-pubkey-one-user makes the lookup unambiguous), then persists (guardian_user_id, child_user_id, consent_jws, consented_at) — the artifact IS the consent record per Hard Rule #13. Count 10 (significant): legally-weighted attestation gating a minor's platform access, though platform blast-radius is low (activates one account; revocable). ACTIVATION GATE: consumer-side enforcement of this flow does NOT go live until counsel review of the consent language + age-tier legal posture completes — the manifest entry ships the substrate ahead of the legal green light. V2 trajectory: when multi-profile v2.0 matures, the child's identity becomes a DERIVED PROFILE under the guardian's master (BIP-32 child at the profile purpose constant) so the guardian-child relationship is cryptographic at the key level, not only attested — this action's claim shape is forward-compatible with that upgrade (child profile_id slots into cap.scope alongside child_user_id).

consent:parental_revoke.description: Guardian withdraws previously-granted parental consent for a minor's account — the legally-required withdrawal path that completes consent:parental (consent without revocation is not verifiable parental consent under COPPA-adjacent state frameworks). Same self-attested model + cap.scope shape as the grant (child_user_id + platform; consent_version optional on revoke). Consumer verifies against the guardian's bound pubkey, matches the existing consent record's guardian_user_id, marks the consent withdrawn + suspends the minor account per the consumer's own policy (suspend-not-delete; data handling per the consumer's retention policy). Count 1 (Tier 0 shape): authority-REMOVING, strictly safer than the grant it reverses, sister of devices:pairing_revoke's posture.

devices:pair.description: Bind the operator's (or end-user's) master enclave pubkey to a downstream consumer's user-account via an 8-char pairing code the consumer minted server-side and the user typed on the phone. Requires the cap.scope.pairing_code extension field (short typed string, NOT a Guid — distinct from chat:* / agents:* whose scope fields are all Guids) binding the JWS to the SPECIFIC code the user typed. Phase H phone-side smoke (2026-05-19 night) — first end-user-fired capability action; the FIRST manifest entry not gated by the operator-pubkey trust root (verifier on the consumer side recovers the signature against the caller-supplied master_pubkey rather than the operator's banked pubkey — self-attested model). Low-blast-radius (binds an identifier; doesn't mint authority of its own; consumer can revoke the binding at any time), single-shot per code (code is consumed on completion), short expiry (~5min). Tier 0 weight reflects the low-risk / one-shot / user-initiated shape. Future Tier-2/3 sibling devices:pair-with-quorum may emerge if end-users want multi-device or multi-pubkey pairing semantics — currently not planned.

devices:pairing_revoke.description: Revoke (unpair) a previously-established devices:pair binding between the user's master enclave pubkey and a downstream consumer's user-account. Phase H follow-on (2026-06-21) — the cryptographic completion of Recto Phone's per-service unpair (Build 6 shipped local-only removal; this makes the consumer-side binding teardown end-to-end). Sister of devices:pair: the phone signs a JWS with cap.allow_actions of devices:pairing_revoke plus a cap.scope.user_id binding naming the specific consumer user-account being unpaired, POSTs it to the bootloader's POST /v0.4/devices/unpair thin-relay, which forwards to the consumer's /api/v1/devices/pairing/revoke. Self-attested verification: the consumer recovers the JWS signature against the master pubkey currently bound on that user row (commitment #11, one-pubkey-one-user, makes the row lookup unambiguous) and NULLs the binding on a match — mirroring devices:pair's self-attested model rather than the operator-pubkey trust root. Tier 0 (count 1): user-initiated, idempotent, authority-REMOVING (strictly safer than the grant it reverses), one-shot. Demo-service unpairs skip this entirely — there is no remote binding to tear down.

scene:compose.description: Compose / revise a 3D scene manifest from a natural-language prompt in a downstream consumer's Scene Composer (the consumer's ComposeSceneTool, 2026-06-10). A compose is a pure manifest-JSON mutation — zero spend, fully undoable client-side (Class A per the consumer's SaaU hot-reload-vs-recompile fork). Tier 1 SESSION-WINDOW semantics: one phone-tap approval covers ~1 hour of compose iterations (cap.exp = now + 3600s), sister of the SaaU code:hot_write session-window posture. The LLM compose context carries the consumer's asset catalog + Knowledge-module classifications for any anchored Media IP (labels + provenance only, never source text per the consumer's Hard Rule #13).

scene:publish.description: RESERVED-DEFERRED — promote a composed scene manifest to a citable signed artifact in a downstream consumer's citation economy (per the consumer's portable-signed-artifacts commitment #15). Registered 2026-06-10 so the action key exists when the consumer-side endpoint ships; NO tool builds claims for it yet and it is intentionally EXCLUDED from every group until then (sister of profile:rotate_master's no-group-grant posture, though for a deferred-not-catastrophic reason).

secret:read.description: Read a secret from Recto's vault

manifest:add-action.description: Add a new action / group to the capability action manifest

scene:asset_generate.description: Generate a NEW 3D asset (text-to-3D via Meshy / Tripo / Blockade-class providers) into a downstream consumer's scene-asset library. Tier 2 PER-ACTION approval (cap.exp ~60s, one approval per generation) because each invocation spends real generation-provider money AND debits 1 THRU per the consumer's image-gen-as-universal-substrate commitment #29 (debit-at-compute semantics). Distinct from scene:compose which only arranges EXISTING catalog assets — generation mints new platform assets with per-creator attribution that persist in the catalog regardless of whether the requester keeps them.

agents:create.description: Create a new agent identity in a downstream consumer's privilege graph. Requires the cap.scope.create_for_owner extension field (Guid) declaring the entity the new agent's owner pins to. Used by orchestrator-DARWIN at downstream-consumer civic-bootstrap (creates the elected public-face agent row owned by the operator at Phase 1 / DAO multi-sig at Phase 6+). Privilege-graph integrity: holders of agents:create CANNOT use it to escalate their own scope — the new agent's allow_actions are bounded by what the operator approves at phone-tap-time, never by the creator's scope. Project-Page-DARWIN (and any future elected agent) structurally CANNOT hold agents:create — the privilege graph has no cycles.

profile:create.description: Mint a new child profile (personal:child / work / school / contractor / custom) under the operator's master enclave key. Master signs an attestation over the candidate profile's metadata + derived pubkey; bootloader stores the row in master_identity.json. Phone-tap approval each invocation — operator sees the kind + display_name + derivation path on the approval card. Phase 2.0.B foundation; v2.0.C extends to multi-device pairing per profile.

profile:add_device.description: Pair a new device to an existing profile. Operator phone-tap approves the binding. Lower weight than profile:create because the trust set is being EXPANDED within an existing profile, not minting fresh authority. v2.0.C target.

profile:revoke_device.description: Revoke a previously-paired device from a profile. Operator phone-tap approves on a still-paired device. In-flight capabilities signed by the revoked device's key continue to verify until their exp, but no new capabilities can be signed by it. v2.0.C target.

profile:rotate_master.description: Catastrophic-tier master rotation — re-derive every profile under the master from a new BIP-39 mnemonic. Old profile keys are retired. Always requires fresh operator approval, no caching. v2.0+ target; aliased to operator-key:rotate at the implementation layer.

secret:write-non-sensitive.description: Write a non-sensitive secret to vault (e.g., config rotation)

secret:rotate.description: Rotate a sensitive secret in the vault

auth-gate:modify.description: Modify an authentication gate or policy

capability:revoke-other.description: Revoke a capability issued to another agent

windows:run_powershell.description: Run an arbitrary PowerShell command on the operator's Windows host (an orchestrator agent's PowerShell tool). Catastrophic-weight, per-command operator-phone approval — the operator sees the exact command on the approval card and taps to approve that ONE command; no session window. Registry, Process, FileSystem, and Windows-service control are all reachable through it. Intentionally in NO group (standalone phone-tap each invocation, like profile:rotate_master).

treasury:transfer.description: Initiate a transfer from an on-chain treasury contract

operator-key:rotate.description: Rotate the operator's signing key — catastrophic-tier authority

darwin:doc-edits._doc: Tier 0 — always autonomous, both staging and prod

darwin:staging-deploys._doc: Tier 1 — autonomous to staging, human-confirm to prod

darwin:secret-reads._doc: Tier 1 — read-only secret access for staging operations

darwin:staging-feature-flags._doc: Tier 1 — flip feature flags in staging only

darwin:registry-curation._doc: Tier 1 — manage the capability action manifest itself

operator:agent-creation._doc: Tier 2 — civic-bootstrap of new agent identities. Per-action operator-phone approval at downstream consumer bootstrap. Carries cap.scope.create_for_owner=<Guid> declaring the entity the new agent's owner pins to. Reserved for orchestrator-DARWIN at Phase 1; the future user-published-agents store reuses the same action key but fires it from each user's authoring surface (operator still approves the scope).

operator:profile-management._doc: Tier 2 — profile lifecycle operations under the operator's master enclave key. Phone-tap approval each invocation. profile:rotate_master is deliberately EXCLUDED from this group — it's catastrophic-tier and always requires standalone phone confirmation, no group-grant shortcut. v2.0.B foundation (profile:create); v2.0.C extends to multi-device add/revoke.

operator:chat-replies._doc: Tier 1 — capability-bounded autonomous chat replies by an elected public-face agent in a downstream consumer (e.g. the consumer's elected Project-Page agent per chat-tier civic-office model Phase F). Each JWS carries a cap.scope.chat_room_id binding to ONE specific ChatRoom — the operator approves a reply IN A SPECIFIC ROOM, not a blanket post-anywhere capability. Sister of darwin:public-comms but for downstream-consumer chat surfaces rather than operator-comms-tunnel replies.

operator:scene-composition._doc: Tier 1/2 mixed — 3D Scene Composer agent surface in a downstream consumer (the consumer's ComposeSceneTool, 2026-06-10). scene:compose is Tier 1 session-window (zero-spend manifest mutation, one approval covers ~1h of iterations); scene:asset_generate is Tier 2 per-action (real provider spend + 1 THRU debit per generation). scene:publish is deliberately NOT in this group — reserved-deferred until the consumer ships the manifest-to-citable-artifact endpoint. Scene tools never acquire agents:* / chat:* / treasury:* / secret rotation authority — the structural deny-prefix posture is enforced consumer-side (SceneCapability delegates to the SaaU deny-prefix list).

operator:chat-tier-promotions._doc: Tier 2 — capability-bounded autonomous civic-office tier promotion in a downstream consumer. Phase F follow-on (2026-05-18). Each JWS carries a cap.scope.target_user_id binding to ONE specific user being promoted — the operator approves a promotion FOR A SPECIFIC USER, not a blanket promote-anyone capability. Higher tier than operator:chat-replies because promotion is a structural civic-office election event (granting authority to post in shared social space) — qualitative DARWIN-curation; never mechanical. Sister actions chat:promote_user_to_tier_2 + chat:demote_to_tier_0 (reserved) will join this group as the chat-tier civic-office model matures.

user:device-pairing._doc: Tier 0 — end-user-fired binding (and teardown) of master enclave pubkey to/from a downstream consumer's user-account. Phase H (devices:pair 2026-05-19; devices:pairing_revoke 2026-06-21). The FIRST group not prefixed `operator:*` or `darwin:*` — denotes capabilities that an end-user (not the platform operator) holds and exercises from their own Recto Phone. devices:pair's JWS carries cap.scope.pairing_code (the 8-char code the user typed); devices:pairing_revoke's JWS carries cap.scope.user_id (the consumer account being unpaired). Both use the self-attested verification model — the consumer recovers the signature against the master pubkey (for pair, the caller-supplied pubkey; for revoke, the pubkey already bound on the user row), not against the operator's banked pubkey — distinct from operator-bounded action surfaces. Future sibling end-user actions (e.g. user:profile-rotate) will join this group as Phase J+ end-user surfaces mature.

user:guardian-consent._doc: End-user family (sister of user:device-pairing) — verifiable parental consent for minors' (13-15) accounts on downstream consumer platforms, granted + withdrawn from the guardian's own Recto Phone. Banked 2026-07-11 per operator directive to commit the 13-15 tier now (extend-down-later is a feature release; walking back up would be a retraction). Both actions use the self-attested verification model recovered against the GUARDIAN's user-row-bound master pubkey — the guardian's paired adult account is the trust anchor, not the operator's banked pubkey. The consent JWS is the canonical legal artifact per Hard Rule #13 (artifact-as-canonical-record): portable, auditable, revocable, QR-able. Consumer-side activation is COUNSEL-GATED — substrate ships ahead of the legal green light so no phone-binary or manifest change blocks the eventual tier launch. V2 trajectory: guardian-child becomes a derived-profile relationship under multi-profile v2.0 (cryptographic at the key level).

operator:high-stakes-ops._doc: Tier 2/3 boundary — sensitive secret rotation, auth gates, billing

operator:catastrophic._doc: Tier 3 — always fresh operator approval, no caching
